items.title: Nepal Floods: School children reunited with families after being stranded – Save the Children
items.summary: Country: Nepal Source: Save the Children KATHMANDU, 28 August 2026 – Nine school children have been reunited with their families after being stranded at school for two days by the devastating flash floods in Northern Nepal, as rescue efforts continue to reach other students, Save the Children said. The children arrived at an aid distribution point where Save the Children is working after walking from their school. Many children in the area travel long distances to their schools and were cut off in the aftermath of the massive surge of floodwater. items.title: WVI Nepal Declares Category I National Response to Flash Floods in Rasuwa and Nuwakot
items.summary: Country: Nepal Source: World Vision A major flash flood entered Nepal through the Bhote Koshi River at around 9:00 AM on 26 August, causing significant damage in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts. Rescue and relief operations are underway, and authorities have issued alerts for communities along the Trishuli River. items.title: Nepal: A newly formed lake is sparking fears of more flooding along the Chinese border

items.title: Nepal flash floods: 'Very challenging' for survivors who have lost their homes and their families
items.summary: Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Sunita Sharma, Head of Programs of Karuna-Shechen. While Nepal has considerable experience responding to natural disasters, the scale of the present devastation exposes a deeper challenge: Placing greater emphasis on preparedness. The immediate priorities are clear: finding those still missing and providing survivors with drinking water, food, shelter, clothing and medicine. But recovery cannot end there. Ultimately, they will need to rebuild confidence and entire communities. Given the scale of the destruction, that process could take years.

items.title: Nepal flood disaster reconstructed minute by minute
items.summary: New satellite imagery and video analysis show the deadly Nepal floods began when part of a glacier near the Chinese border collapsed, triggering a debris flow that raced downstream at up to 150 km/h and devastated communities over more than 80 kilometres. Scientists are still piecing together the exact sequence of events, while authorities warn the disaster may not be over as a newly formed lake upstream has started to overflow.
